newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Profit-taking sends Seoul shrs sharply lower close.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking sends Seoul shrs sharply lower close.

text.p: Stocks closed sharply lower on Friday on widespread profit-taking after rising over the past week, brokers said.
The current wave of strikes was no longer seen giving a major impact on the market, they said.
The composite index ended at a provisional 701.18, down 1.5 percent or 10.68 points, after touching an intra-day low of 695.77. It touched a high of 720.41.
Decliners overwhelmed advancing stocks by 609 to 224.

"Sentiment seems to remain bullish as customer deposits continue to increase," said Koh Soon-shik of LG Securities. "But many investors appeared to believe market will not be able to go further without undergoing some correction."

The market rose by more than 16 percent since the middle of last week, at first on the back of speculation that mergers and acquisitions would become active among banks and then due to expectations of increasing foreign buying.
The current wave of strikes, that started late last year in protest at the passage of a new labour law, has already been fully discounted, brokers said.

Blue chips fell across the board, with the exception of Korea Electric Power and Dacom Corp. Korea Electric rose 300 won to 28,600 on steady foreign buying and Dacom gained 6,000 won to 105,000 in line with the strength of telecom stocks.

Small-capitalised stocks perceived to be undervalued were among the main gainers. Doosan Machinery rose 620 won to its daily limit of 8,370 and Daelim Trading closed at its upper limit of 21,600 by rising 1,600.
